burn verb

be on fire

also be burning, be alight, burning

classical

Cic. Div. 1.121: caput ārsisse
Juv. 3.201: ultimus ārdēbit (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 315

ārdeō, ārdēre, ārsī, ārsum

verb, second conjugation

burn, be on fire, blaze

Of anything alight: a house, a torch, a fire. Also, as in English, of fever, anger and love (ārdēre amōre). Setting something on fire is incendere or ūrere (see burn, set fire to).

Examples

  • Caput ārsisse Serviō Tulliō dormientī quae historia nōn prōdidit?

    What history doesn’t tell how Servius Tullius’s head was on fire while he slept?Cic. Div. 1.121

See also fire, burn, burn, flame, smoke.

SourcesLewis & Short: ardeo
